question: Refer to the exhibit. A vPC pair connects to two firewalls, ASA_1 and ASA_2, through orphan ports. When one of the vPC peer links goes down, the orphan ports connected to the firewalls remain up, and traffic continues to be forwarded to the firewall that is connected to the switch with the failed link, causing traffic loss. Which action resolves this issue?
context: Topology: vPC pair of switches connected to ASA_1 and ASA_2 firewalls via orphan (non-vPC) ports.
imageNote: Diagram: vPC pair of switches, ASA_1 connected to the left switch and ASA_2 to the right switch via orphan ports; the two switches form a vPC domain and both connect down to a shared server.
options: Configure the vPC peer-switch feature on both switches.
Activate the vPC orphan-port suspend feature on the switch ports connected to the firewall.
Configure a static route to redirect traffic away from the affected switch.
Enable the vPC auto-recovery feature on both switches.
theory: When a device is single-homed to only one member of a vPC pair, it becomes an orphan port, and losing the vPC peer link doesn't automatically bring that orphan port down — so traffic can keep arriving at a switch that has lost synchronization with its vPC peer and can no longer forward it correctly. The vPC orphan-port suspend feature is designed to shut down the orphan port when the peer link fails, forcing the firewall to fail over to its still-healthy connection on the other switch instead of black-holing traffic; peer-switch and auto-recovery address different failure scenarios (shared STP root identity and peer-link/keepalive recovery), not orphan-port traffic loss. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 2 — vPC Orphan Ports and Failure Handling)
